$comment: GENERATED by scripts/units/year/type-work-list.js. Never edit by hand.

A.title: Read a little book with a pattern
A.differs: 7 English picture readers (I See Pets, At the Farm, My Lunch ...): cover + three pages of one patterned sentence each; K-630 is the same book to colour, K-631 the Read and Talk companion page.

A.title: Vowels and consonants
A.differs: K-230 sorts letters into vowels and consonants; K-533 colours every vowel in picture words (L1 four 3-5-letter words), the second half of the objective.

A.title: Read a decodable book
A.differs: 5 English decodable mini-books (Dad and Sam, Kit and the Dog ...), every word gated to the taught sounds and heart words, no pictures: the child reads each page and draws it; K-631 is the companion page.

A.title: The pictures and the words
A.differs: Level 1 (one story of four sentences): the child numbers the sentences and draws a line from each to its picture. The 'stories' are four-step picture sequences (an apple eaten bite by bite, a fence being painted), not a tale with characters; the teacher reads the sentences.

A.title: Find the answer in the story
A.differs: Level 1: a 43-73-word story with numbered sentences and 3 literal questions (who, what, where, when, why), each with a 'Sentence N' chip that sends the child to the sentence holding the answer. 3 multiple-choice questions, not 4; the stories are not strictly decodable (pumpkins, librarian); the child is shown the sentence rather than underlining it. G1-504 asks the same passages as open questions on lines (3/4/5 questions).

A.title: Two texts on one topic
A.differs: The ready material of the grade-2 point (en-2-078) serves here too: two printed animal fact files (class, habitat, diet, covering), circle same or different for each fact, then write two things that are the same and two that are different. The 'texts' are fact-file tables, not 40-word running texts, and there is no fact-strip sort level.

A.title: Compound words and two-part words
A.differs: G2-330 Split the Compound (draw a line where the second word starts; L1 shows the parts) = level 1; G1-324 Syllable Cards (read the word one syllable at a time, L1 two syllables) = level 2 (rabbit, picnic); G2-332 Compound Detective (12 words, circle the 6 compounds and write their parts) = level 3. Three pages, not one; no picture of each small word.

A.title: Two animals: same and different
A.source: reuse:Compare Two Animals: Same and Different

A.title: Root words as clues
A.differs: G3-399 Root Words in Sentences writes four family words above a root stone into sentence gaps (meaning from the shared root); G2-359 sorts derived words onto their roots; G2-375 finds the shared root. Eight English families (help, play, care, use, joy, fear, act, sleep); the child shows the meaning by using the word, not by writing a definition.

A.title: Past tense: regular and irregular verbs
A.differs: Level 2/3: a table of six pictured verbs (today form and past) + sentence gaps; the 28-verb bank has regular (jumped, hopped, carried, giggled) and irregular pasts (ran, slept, threw, caught, built, hid). G2-337 chooses the form in a sentence, G2-334 matches verbs to past forms. No regular/irregular mark column, no present-tense story to rewrite.

use.title: Ask and answer questions about a fact text
use.differs: There is no information-text-with-questions page. The nearest is G2-343 Who Am I? Mystery Animal: three cards of five first-person fact clues and a bank of six animal pictures (answer = the animal: a picture choice). It answers 'who am I', not who/what/where/how questions about a 30-word fact text, and is G2 reading. Far: an information-text bank (30-80 words per grade) with picture-answer questions.
use.note: built: Find the Facts, a fact text of four sentences in big print; four questions answered by circling one of three pictures, by drawing, or by drawing and asking a question of their own

use.title: What is it all about? The main topic
use.differs: G2-488 Which Title Fits?: two passages without titles, circle the title that fits of three: the main-topic idea. The passages are narrative stories (30-73 words), not information texts, the answers are printed titles (no pictures), and there are no key-detail boxes. Needs an information-text bank.
use.note: built: What Is It All About?, the same texts; circle the picture of the whole text, then circle or draw its key details

use.title: Pictures that teach
use.differs: Science-catalogue types. G2-364 Parts of a Plant and Their Functions: five job phrases (root 'takes in water from the soil', stem, leaf, flower, seed) matched to numbered tags on a plant picture by writing the tag number: the text-to-picture link the lesson teaches. One level only (five parts), phrases not a four-sentence text, numbered tags instead of word labels; G1-376 labels the parts from a word bank (the level-3 'add a label'). Small change: a 2-/4-label K ladder and a line-drawing answer.
use.note: built: Pictures That Teach, a line from each sentence of a fact text to the picture that goes with it (three sentences, four, four with one picture to draw); the labeled plant picture of the design gave way to the pictures of each text

use.title: First this, then that: connect two ideas
use.differs: Science-catalogue types. G1-203 The Life Cycle of a Chicken: number three pictures 1-2-3 (egg to chick, the need's own example); G1-377 the butterfly. There is no information text to read and no 'First ___, then ___' frame; it sequences pictures rather than connecting two ideas in a text. Small change for the picture part; the text needs an information-text bank.
use.note: built: First, Then, a fact text that tells a change, a question that names it, and two boxes joined by an arrow (cut and glue, draw, draw and write a word)

use.title: Ask and answer: facts in the text
use.differs: G1-504 Read and Answer has the right shape (a passage, 3/4/5 key-detail questions with answer lines) but its passages are narrative stories (30-73 words), not information texts with a heading and a picture; G2-343 reads animal fact clues. Moderate: an information-text bank (about 70 words) for the G1-504/G2-254 pages; the question formats exist.
use.note: built: Read the Facts, an informational text of about 60 words with two headed parts; four questions to circle, to finish from a starter, or to write and underline in the text

use.title: The main topic and key details
use.differs: G2-488 Which Title Fits?: two untitled passages, circle the title of three (main topic). Narrative stories, not information texts; no key-detail boxes. Needs an information-text bank.
use.note: built: Main Topic and Key Details on the same texts (circle the topic and copy a detail; write the topic and two or three key details)

use.title: Text features: headings, bold words, a glossary
use.differs: No text-features page exists (no text with headings, bold words, captions or a glossary anywhere in the banks). Build an information-text bank with marked features and a find-it question page.
use.note: built (nothing was close): Use the Text Features, find-it questions from headings, bold words, caption and glossary, with G1-578 Name the Text Features as the page before it

use.title: The main topic of a text and of each paragraph
use.differs: G2-488 picks the title that fits a whole passage (main topic) but its passages are one-paragraph narrative stories (30-73 words); no three-paragraph information text, no per-paragraph focus. Needs an information-text bank.
use.note: built: Main Topic and Paragraphs, an informational text of about 150 words as three numbered paragraphs without title or headings; circle the main topic and give each statement its paragraph, or write topic and focus, or also a heading

use.title: Text features: captions, bold words, glossary, index
use.differs: No text with captions, bold words, subheadings, a glossary or an index exists. Build an information-text bank with marked features and a find-it question page.
use.note: built (nothing was close): Glossary and Index, the same texts as a small book page with headings, bold words, two captioned pictures, a glossary and an index; six find-it questions to circle or to write, and on the hardest level an index entry and a glossary entry to add

use.title: What the diagram shows
use.differs: Science-catalogue types. G2-365 Label the Butterfly Life Cycle: write the four stage names from a bank under their pictures and cross out the name that does not belong; G1-377 numbers the stages. No 120-word text and no questions answered from the diagram or from text + diagram. Moderate: a short text + diagram questions on the G2-365 layout.
use.note: built (the science page was not close enough): What the Diagram Shows, a text of two paragraphs and a cycle diagram of drawn stages with labels and arrows; questions from the diagram, what the diagram adds, a label and an arrow to add; with G2-524 Text or Diagram? as its second page

use.title: Steps in order: how it is made
use.differs: G2-378 Retell with Starters writes a 4-step process sequence (making a sandwich, painting a fence, building a snowman) with First / Next / Then / Finally; G1-402 orders the sentences of a sequence. Pictures, not a 150-word how-it-is-made information text, and no 'why must this step come first'. Moderate: process texts on the same layouts.
use.note: built: Steps in Order, a how-it-is-made text of four steps (First, Next, Then, Finally) with three pictures; number the steps, write them in a flow chart, tell why one step comes before another; with G2-525 Before and After as its second page

K-548.title: In, on, under, next to
K-548.differs: Maths-catalogue type (K.G.A.1, Position Words maker). K-548 level 1: in, on top of, under, next to; level 3 adds behind and in front of (circle the word that fits the sentence for each scene). The relation is a picture and a shape, not a cat and a box. K-546 (published) is the need's level 3: read the sentence and draw the picture in place.

G1-493.title: Blends at the start: st, fl, tr
G1-493.differs: Initial blends (bl br cl cr dr fl fr gl gr pl pr sk sl sm sn sp st sw tr tw; 57 pictures): L1 circle the blend of three, L2 write the two letters before the printed rest (__og), L3 from the picture. A page spreads over all blends (no s-blends-only level 1), about a third of the words have two or more syllables (bracelet, broccoli, dragonfly), and there is no read-and-match half. G1-333 adds blend word-family ladders.

G1-495.unit: Long Vowels: Silent e and Vowel Teams
G1-495.title: Long or short vowel?
G1-495.differs: Level 1 (six one-syllable words): the child says each word and circles the long line or the short dot. The word is printed with its vowel coloured (the spelling shows the length) and all vowels mix; there is no cut-and-sort into two boxes and no one-vowel level.

G1-495.title: Short or long vowel?
G1-495.differs: Level 2 (eight one-syllable words) or level 3 (two-syllable words too): say the word, circle the long line or the short dot; long = silent e or ai ay ee oa igh ie. Marking, not sorting into two columns; no hop/hope sentence choice.

G1-506.title: Plan a story: characters, setting, problem
G1-506.differs: Level 3: Beginning (Who is in the story? Where are they?), Problem (What goes wrong?), Middle (What happens?), End (How does it end?), each with a drawing box and 2 lines. One middle box (not three events), no story-mountain picture, no checklist.

K-628.title: Read left to right, top to bottom
K-628.differs: The mini-books practise tracking in a real book: K-629 'point under each word as you read', page by page; K-628 pages break over 2-3 lines ("Kit the cat | sat on a mat."), so the return sweep happens. No page prints start/stop dots or left-to-right and return-sweep arrows to trace or draw, and none asks to number the words. New layout (print-concepts page), not a small change.
K-628.note: New layout (print-concepts page), not a small change

K-552.title: One spoken word, one written word
K-552.differs: K-552 Sentence Strips prints 2-4 picture sentences as one word card per word that the child cuts apart and rebuilds (one card = one word), and K-629 has the child point under each word; neither has the row of empty boxes to colour one per spoken word, nor the 3-word / 4-5-word sentence ladder. Small change: a box row under each K-552 sentence.
K-552.note: a box row under each K-552 sentence

K-552.title: Spaces between words: count the words
K-552.differs: K-552 makes the word boundaries physical (cut the sentence into word cards); K-527 Trace a Sentence has the child copy a sentence (finger spaces). Nothing asks to draw a line in each space, count the words and write the number. Small change: a count-the-words mode over the K-552/K-527 sentence bank.
K-552.note: a count-the-words mode over the K-552/K-527 sentence bank

G1-314.title: Blend the first sound and the rest
G1-314.differs: G1-314 Blend the Sounds prints the word's sounds in boxes (L1 3-4 sounds) and the child blends them and circles the matching picture of three. It is phoneme-by-phoneme blending from PRINTED letters, not oral onset-rime blending the teacher says (/s/ ... /un/), and it has no levels by distractor kind (different first sound / same first sound / same rime). Moderate change: an oral 'teacher says it' mode with no letters and rime-controlled picture triples.
G1-314.note: change: an oral 'teacher says it' mode with no letters and rime-controlled picture triples

K-227.title: Short a and short i
K-227.differs: K-227 Middle Sounds: CVC pictures, the child writes the middle vowel; K-224: write the missing (vowel) letter. Both mix all five vowels on every page and cannot be limited to short a / short i; the K-227 bank holds 18 words (a 6, i 3, o 4, u 3, e 2), too few for twelve words of one vowel. No read-the-word-and-match half, no two-column sort. G1-306 has -an and -at families (onset writing). Small-to-moderate change: a vowel unit axis + a larger CVC bank.
K-227.note: Small-to-moderate change: a vowel unit axis + a larger CVC bank

K-227.title: Short o, short u, and short e
K-227.differs: Same as en-K-008: the medial-vowel pages mix all vowels and the bank is thin (o 4, u 3, e 2 words in K-227); no one-vowel page, no read-and-match half, no two-column sort. Needs a vowel unit axis and a larger CVC bank.
K-227.note: Needs a vowel unit axis and a larger CVC bank

G1-330.title: Which word matches: cat or cot?
G1-330.differs: G1-330 Word Families: Read and Circle shows a picture and a column of words from the same rime row (can / fan / pan / van) and the child circles the one that names it: real words differing in the FIRST letter only (the need's level 1). Nothing pairs words differing in the last letter or the middle vowel (cat/cot, pin/pen), and nothing asks to underline the letter that differs. G1-552 compares a word with misspellings (non-words). Small change: a minimal-pair bank with first/last/middle levels.
G1-330.note: a minimal-pair bank with first/last/middle levels

G1-506.title: Who is in the story, and where?
G1-506.differs: G1-506 Story Map is the organiser (L1 boxes Beginning 'Who is in the story? Where are they?', Middle 'What happens?', End, each with a draw box and 2 lines) for any read-aloud, but it prints no story and has no picture choices. G2-254's stories (30-73 words, narratives) ask who/where among 3 word-choice questions, not pictures. Moderate: a read-aloud picture-panel story bank + Who/Where/What-happened boxes.
G1-506.note: a read-aloud picture-panel story bank + Who/Where/What-happened boxes

G1-506.unit: Draw and Write: Opinions, Facts, and Stories
G1-506.title: What happened to me: a small moment
G1-506.differs: G1-506 Story Map L1: beginning / middle / end boxes with a draw box and 2 lines each, prompts about a story (Who is in the story?), not a personal small moment. Missing the two picture boxes First/Then, the frames First I ___. Then I ___. I felt ___., the word bank and the checklist. Small change in writing-frames.js.

G1-506.title: Characters, setting, and big events
G1-506.differs: G1-506 is a story map but its boxes are beginning / middle / end (L3 + problem), not characters / setting / big events, and it prints no story; G2-254 prints stories (43-73 words) whose questions touch who and where but carry no story map. Small change: a characters-setting-events box set in G1-506 + a story from the G2-254 pools.
G1-506.note: a characters-setting-events box set in G1-506 + a story from the G2-254 pools

G1-506.title: Write a true story: plan and draft
G1-506.differs: G1-506 Story Map plans a story (beginning / middle / end boxes with prompts, draw box + 2-3 lines); G2-378 writes a picture sequence with First / Next / Then / Finally starters. No true-story planner with first/next/last + a 6-line draft page, no time-word frames on every line, no checklist. Small change in writing-frames.js.

G1-506.title: Plan and draft a true story
G1-506.differs: G1-506 Story Map L3 (beginning / problem / middle / end, draw box + 2 lines each) plans a story; G2-378 drafts a picture sequence with time-word starters. No who-and-where / feelings planner for a personal small moment, no 10-line draft page, no checklist. Small change in writing-frames.js.

G1-506.title: How a story begins and ends
G1-506.differs: G1-506 Story Map L3 (beginning / problem / middle / end) is the arc organizer; G1-401 draws the middle between a beginning and an end. Neither prints a story (~150 words) or asks what the beginning introduces and how the end solves the problem. Moderate: a story bank with the arc questions.
G1-506.note: a story bank with the arc questions

K-381.title: Retell the story: beginning, middle, end
K-381.differs: K-381 is the need's level 1 (cut out three pictures, glue them in First / Next / Last; L1 one strip), G1-401 the level-2 drawing (draw the middle between the given beginning and end). But the strips are wordless object-change sequences (an apple eaten, a fence painted), not a story with characters read aloud, and there is no retell frame (First ___. Then ___.). Moderate: a read-aloud story bank on the same layouts.
K-381.note: a read-aloud story bank on the same layouts

G2-254.title: Ask and answer questions about a story
G2-254.differs: G2-254 has stories the teacher can read (L2 published pool 44-73 words) with 3 key-detail questions (who, what, where, why, how does X feel) but the answers are three printed WORDS/phrases, which a kindergartner cannot read; no picture answers and no own-question box. Moderate: picture-answer questions for a short read-aloud story.
G2-254.note: picture-answer questions for a short read-aloud story

G2-254.title: How characters meet a challenge
G2-254.differs: G2-254 level 3: 2 inference questions + 1 written answer about stories with a small problem (a tower washed away, a stuck ball) and 'How does X feel?' questions. Stories are 58-73 words (not ~150), there is no challenge / what-the-character-did / feeling organizer and no quote-as-proof. Moderate: longer stories + an organizer layout.

G2-254.title: Show where the story says it
G2-254.differs: G2-254 level 1 numbers the sentences and points each literal question to its sentence (evidence), level 3 adds a written answer. Stories are one paragraph of 58-73 words (need ~250 words in numbered paragraphs), 3 questions, no box for the proving paragraph, no copying the exact words. Moderate: longer grade-3 stories in the same Level Set format.
G2-254.note: longer grade-3 stories in the same Level Set format

G2-254.title: Characters: traits, feelings, and actions
G2-254.differs: Some G2-254 pool questions ask about traits and feelings ('What kind of brother is Yusuf?', 'How does Zara feel?'); G1-509 describes a pictured character with adjectives. No 250-word story with a changing character, no character web with proof lines, no cause-and-effect chain. Moderate.
G2-254.note: No 250-word story with a changing character, no character web with proof lines, no cause-and-effect chain

G2-254.unit: Information Texts: Main Idea and Text Features
G2-254.title: Answer with evidence from an information text
G2-254.differs: The question shape exists (G2-254 L1 points each question to its numbered sentence; G1-504 open answers) but all passages are narrative stories of 30-73 words: no 250-word information text with headings, photo and numbered paragraphs, no paragraph-number box. Needs an information-text bank.

G1-293.title: Naming words and action words
G1-293.differs: G1-293 Nouns and Verbs: Two Bins, level 1: 3 nouns + 3 verbs, the nouns with a small picture, the child copies each word into the naming or the doing bin. The verbs have no picture (a kindergartner cannot read them), the child writes rather than cuts and pastes, and there is no 'The ___ can ___.' frame. Small change: action pictures (library 'activities' theme) and a cut-and-sort mode.
G1-293.note: action pictures (library 'activities' theme) and a cut-and-sort mode

G1-498.title: A sentence starts with a capital letter
G1-498.differs: G1-498 prints sentences in small letters only and the child circles every word that needs a capital: the first word, the word I and names (L1 four sentences, L3 rewrite). Sentences are 5-8 words (not 3), names are mixed in, and no page prints mostly correct sentences with a few small-letter starts to fix. Small change: a K level with 3-4-word sentences and no names.
G1-498.note: a K level with 3-4-word sentences and no names

G1-498.title: Names, days, and months get capitals
G1-498.differs: G1-498 Capital Letters: sentences in small letters, circle each word needing a capital (first word, names, I; L3 rewrite). Its 18 sentences hold names only; the generator states that weekdays and months are not in them. No date or own-name writing. Small change: sentences with days and months.

G1-498.title: Capitals for holidays, places, and brand names
G1-498.differs: G1-498 is the circle-the-capitals page, but its sentences carry only names, I and the first word; no holidays, places or product names, and no needs-a-capital sort. Small change: a sentence set tagged for holidays / places / brands.
G1-498.note: a sentence set tagged for holidays / places / brands

G1-498.title: Capitals in titles
G1-498.differs: G1-498 is the circle-the-words-needing-a-capital page (L3 rewrite) but for sentence capitals and names; no titles and no rule that a, the, of, in stay small. Small change: a title bank with a title-case rule.
G1-498.note: a title bank with a title-case rule

G2-282.title: A period or a question mark?
G2-282.differs: G2-282 level 1: broken sentences (no capital, no end mark, one name) that the child rewrites with a capital and the right end mark, . or ?. It asks a K child to rewrite whole sentences, has no pictures and no half-telling/half-asking structure for writing only the mark. Small change: a 'write only the end mark' K level with pictures.
G2-282.note: a 'write only the end mark' K level with pictures

G2-282.title: Revise and edit a story with a checklist
G2-282.differs: Only the editing part exists: G2-282 / G2-274 rewrite broken single sentences (capital, names, end mark) with a checklist banner. No sample story with mixed mistakes, no revise checks (detail, stronger word, word-wall spelling), no checklist for the own draft.
G2-282.note: No sample story with mixed mistakes, no revise checks (detail, stronger word, word-wall spelling), no checklist for the own draft

G1-503.title: Say more: make the sentence longer
G1-503.differs: G1-503 Stretch the Sentence: a short sentence (The big dog plays.), the questions Where? When? (How? from L2) with a line each, then the longer sentence. Same skill (expand with where/when/how) but no picture, no box of add-ons to circle or copy; the child must invent and write the phrases (G1 demand). Small change: a K level with a picture and a printed add-on box.
G1-503.note: a K level with a picture and a printed add-on box

K-554.unit: Draw and Write: Opinions, Facts, and Stories
K-554.title: My favorite and why: an opinion
K-554.differs: K-554 My Reading Log names the book (title, author), rates it with stars, asks 'My favorite part' and a drawing; K-342 has the child circle a favourite picture and copy its word. Neither has the opinion frames 'My favorite ___ is ___. I like it because ___.', a word bank or the 3-icon checklist. Small change: an opinion frame with the writing-frames.js starter blanks.
K-554.note: an opinion frame with the writing-frames.js starter blanks

G1-509.unit: Draw and Write: Opinions, Facts, and Stories
G1-509.title: Teach a fact: draw, label, and write
G1-509.differs: G1-509 Describe the Character: a big picture and the starters My character's name is ___ / is ___ and ___ / likes ___ / lives in ___ with a word bank (L1-2): describing a pictured animal, not the child's own topic, and no labelled drawing box. K-555 gives a picture and one line; G2-318 a fact file of one animal. None prints This is a ___. It has ___. It can ___., a box for a labelled drawing or the checklist. Small change in writing-frames.js.

K-326.title: First, middle, or last sound?
K-326.differs: K-326 Beginning, Middle or End: the child colours the box where the week's letter sound is heard; level 1 = beginning or end only (3-0-3), level 3 = four middle cards: the need's ladder. But the pictures are words of any length (mailbox) and 'middle' is a consonant inside a long word, not the vowel of a CVC/CCVC word; K-227 covers the medial vowel separately. Small change: a one-syllable picture filter and vowel units.
K-326.note: a one-syllable picture filter and vowel units

G2-324.title: ck, ng, and wh
G2-324.differs: Of the three spellings only ck exists: the G2-315 rule 'c, k or ck' (G2-324 Which One?, G2-326 sort) has ck words (sock, lock, duck, rocket) mixed with c/k choices. No ng and no wh unit in any type (G1-311 Sound of the Week has sh, ch, th only). Small change: ng and wh units in data/b3/spelling-rules.js or the letter-of-the-week bank.
G2-324.note: ng and wh units in data/b3/spelling-rules.js or the letter-of-the-week bank

G1-306.title: Blends at the end: nd, mp, st
G1-306.differs: No final-blend bank exists. G1-306 has one final-blend family, -and (hand, sand), among CVC rimes; G1-493 does INITIAL blends only. Small change: a final-blend bank (nd, mp, st, nk) for the G1-493 factory.
G1-306.note: a final-blend bank (nd, mp, st, nk) for the G1-493 factory

K-319.title: Words that show feelings
K-319.differs: K-319 Feelings matches six faces to feeling words (part of level 1); G2-254 asks 'How does X feel?' about its stories. No page has the child underline feeling and sense words in a story or poem, and no sense words appear. Moderate: a short story/poem bank with tagged feeling and sense words.
K-319.note: a short story/poem bank with tagged feeling and sense words

G2-315.unit: Long Vowels: Silent e and Vowel Teams
G2-315.title: Silent e changes the vowel
G2-315.differs: G2-315 unit 'Magic e' (a_e i_e o_e u_e; 48 picture words, L1 3-8 letters): read the rule box, write the vowel and the final e into the gaps. Mostly long words (lemonade, telephone, porcupine), no cap/cape pairs, no 'add an e and read the new word' task, no a_e-only level. Small change: CVC/CVCe pair bank + a vowel-by-vowel level.
G2-315.note: CVC/CVCe pair bank + a vowel-by-vowel level

G2-315.unit: Long Vowels: Silent e and Vowel Teams
G2-315.title: oa and ow
G2-315.differs: The spelling-rules factory has no oa/ow unit (en units: magic-e, c-k-ck, ee-ea, ai-ay, floss, y-ies-f-ves). Small change: an oa-ow rule unit in data/b3/spelling-rules.js; the pages (gap, sort, which one) exist.
G2-315.note: an oa-ow rule unit in data/b3/spelling-rules.js

G2-315.title: oo, ou, ow, oi, and oy
G2-315.differs: The spelling-rules factory (gap, sort, which-one pages) has no oo, ou/ow or oi/oy unit in English. Small change: three rule units in data/b3/spelling-rules.js (with the oi-middle / oy-end and ou-middle / ow-end rule).
